# Shared cross-language vectors for sim/research_schema.lua's canonical
# serializer and fnv1a64 content digest.
#
# Generated from the real Lua implementation (`love .` against a scratch copy
# of core/, data/, and sim/ — see v2/tools/lua_reference/README.md for the
# harness). Asserted from:
#   - Rust: crates/gc-sim/src/research_schema.rs (tests::shared_vectors_agree_with_lua)
#
# Every record-shaped case validates against one shared shape, reproduced
# identically in the Rust test:
#
#   record("research_vector_record/v1", {
#       { name = "id", kind = "id" },
#       { name = "count", kind = "integer" },
#       { name = "flag", kind = "boolean" },
#       { name = "tag", kind = "enum", values = enum({ "alpha", "beta" }) },
#       { name = "digest", kind = "hash" },
#       { name = "note", kind = "text", optional = true },
#       { name = "payload", kind = "string" },
#       { name = "tags", kind = "array", element = { name = "item", kind = "integer" } },
#       { name = "scores", kind = "map", element = { name = "score", kind = "number" } },
#   })
#
# Format: one vector per non-comment, non-blank line, tab-separated:
#   label<TAB>encoded_hex<TAB>digest
# `encoded_hex` is the lowercase hex encoding of research_schema.encode()'s
# raw byte output (kept as hex, not raw bytes, so this file stays plain ASCII
# even though the "non_utf8_byte_in_payload" case's payload deliberately
# contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8). `digest` is the expected
# lowercase fnv1a64 hex digest of those same raw bytes
# (research_schema.content_hash()'s output).
#
# Cases:
#   ordinary_record                  - a normal, fully-populated record,
#                                       whose `scores` map is authored with
#                                       keys out of sorted order (zebra,
#                                       apple, mango) to prove the encoder
#                                       sorts map keys rather than trusting
#                                       Lua's unspecified pairs() order.
#   empty_values                     - an omitted optional `note`, an empty
#                                       array, and an empty map.
#   negative_and_fractional_numbers  - a negative integer, negative and
#                                       fractional map values, and numbers at
#                                       the extreme small/large ends of the
#                                       exponent range (1e17, -1e-17),
#                                       exercising number_bytes's frexp-based
#                                       encoding beyond ordinary values.
#   non_utf8_byte_in_payload         - a `string` field whose value contains
#                                       a raw 0xff byte and an invalid UTF-8
#                                       continuation sequence (0xc3 0x28).
#                                       research_schema rejects Lua control
#                                       characters in string/text fields but
#                                       not non-ASCII/invalid-UTF-8 bytes, so
#                                       this is legal wire content that must
#                                       round-trip as opaque bytes.
#
# Two more lines, generated the same way, pin `research_schema.tuple_hash`
# independent of any record shape:
#   tuple_hash_two_parts  - tuple_hash("research-vector/v1", {"a", "bc"})
#   tuple_hash_numeric    - tuple_hash("research-vector/v1", {1, -2.5})
# For these two, `encoded_hex` is empty (tuple_hash has no separate encode
# step to capture) and only `digest` is meaningful.

ordinary_record		f92ef390a2f62f1a
empty_values		13f8826b8bb9a1b2
negative_and_fractional_numbers		31aef10e77f6819b
non_utf8_byte_in_payload		303e66d6c77eb310
tuple_hash_two_parts		03423e9d1140677a
tuple_hash_numeric		ecf98abf4088039f
